story.title: Story 4: Smart Compact Snapshot And Rollout Regeneration

result.reviewScopeSummary: Reviewed Story 4 against the story spec, full SQLite persistence tech design, and test plan; traced the production smart-compact path through readiness, SQLite compact snapshot reads, projection/materialization, generated-output persistence, and regeneration; then ran focused smart-compact suites plus the configured `npm run verify-all` gate.

newFindings.title: Smart compact can throw on a live SQLite source revision change before it ever reads the compact snapshot
newFindings.evidence: `runSmartCompact(...)` still opens the thread and then acquires a revision-pinned mutation lease before projection (`src/commands/smart-compact.ts:333-349`). `FileThreadMutationCoordinator.acquireThreadLease(...)` throws `StaleThreadMutationError` on source-revision drift instead of returning a structured result (`src/thread/store/mutation-coordinator.ts:72-101`). The new projection path only becomes SQLite-snapshot-based after that point (`src/thread-view/services/thread-view-builder.ts:987-991`). In an ad-hoc SQLite repro on 2026-05-26, appending one message after the initial `openThread()` but before lease acquisition caused `runSmartCompact` to throw `STALE_SOURCE_REVISION` rather than re-read current managed state and compact from `readCompactSnapshot(...)`. Because `npm run verify-all` passed, this regression is currently untested by the story gate.

productionPathFindings: No fake adapter, shim, or placeholder production branch was found in the reviewed SQLite smart-compact path. The blocker is in the real runtime flow: `runSmartCompact` can abort on a stale pre-snapshot lease before it uses the intended SQLite snapshot contract.
additionalObservations: `buildThreadViewProjection(...)` now uses `readCompactSnapshot(...)` and passes that snapshot into `ThreadViewMaterializer`, so the earlier post-snapshot re-read risk is not present in the current workspace.
The configured gate is green; the remaining blocker is a semantic concurrency defect rather than a lint/type/test/build failure.
